title.zh: 卷一百三十 列傳第八十: 王璵 李泌 崔造 關播
title.en: Volume 130 Biographies 80: Wang Yu, Li Bi, Cui Zao, Guan Bo
title.raw: 卷一百三十 列傳第八十: 王璵 李泌 崔造 關播 Volume 130 Biographies 80: Wang Yu, Li Bi, Cui Zao, Guan Bo

sentences.zh: 王玙 道士李國禎附

translations.literal: Wang Yu; appended: the Daoist Li Guozhen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu — with an appended account of the Daoist Li Guozhen

sentences.zh: 李泌 子繁 顧況附

translations.literal: Li Bi; his son Fan; appended: Gu Kuang
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi — with appended accounts of his son Fan and Gu Kuang

sentences.zh: 崔造 關播 李元平附

translations.literal: Cui Zao; Guan Bo; appended: Li Yuanping
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao and Guan Bo — with an appended account of Li Yuanping

sentences.zh: 王玙，少習禮學，博求祠祭儀注以干時。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, in youth studied ritual learning, broadly sought sacrificial rites and regulations to win the times.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu studied ritual learning in his youth and assiduously mastered the regulations governing sacrifice and worship in order to advance himself at court.

sentences.zh: 開元末，玄宗方尊道術，靡神不宗。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era, Emperor Xuanzong was then honoring Daoist arts; no spirit was not revered.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Kaiyuan reign, Emperor Xuanzong was exalting Daoist practices, and there was scarcely a deity he did not honor.

sentences.zh: 玙抗疏引古今祀典，請置春壇，祀青帝於國東郊，玄宗甚然之，因遷太常博士、侍御史，充祠祭使。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a forthright memorial citing ancient and modern sacrificial canons, requesting establishment of a spring altar to sacrifice to the Green Emperor at the state's eastern suburb; Emperor Xuanzong greatly approved, and thereby he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Attending Censor, and appointed Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a bold memorial citing precedents from the sacrificial canon, urging that a spring altar be established to worship the Green Emperor in the eastern suburbs of the capital. The emperor strongly approved, and Yu was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Attending Censor, with appointment as Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites.

sentences.zh: 玙專以祀事希幸，每行祠禱，或焚紙錢，禱祈福祐，近於巫覡，由是過承恩遇。

translations.literal: Yu specialized in using sacrificial affairs to seek favor; whenever he performed temple prayers, he sometimes burned paper money, praying to seek blessings and protection, close to shamans and mediums, and thereby excessively received imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yu made a specialty of currying favor through sacrificial rites. Whenever he conducted prayers at shrines, he would sometimes burn spirit money and petition for divine protection—practices that bordered on shamanism—and in this way he won far more imperial favor than his merits warranted.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，累遷太常卿，以祠禱每多賜賚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, Yu was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; because of sacrificial prayers he often received many bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong came to the throne, Yu rose in succession to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and he received frequent imperial gifts on account of his sacrificial and prayer services.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年七月，兼蒲州刺史，充蒲、同、絳等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Qianyuan, he was concurrently made Prefect of Pu Prefecture and appointed Military Commissioner of Pu, Tong, Jiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qianyuan 3 (760), he was concurrently appointed Prefect of Pu and Military Commissioner over Pu, Tong, Jiang, and the other prefectures in that circuit.

sentences.zh: 中書令崔圓罷相，乃以玙為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister of the Secretariat Cui Yuan was removed as Chancellor, Yu was then made Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Cui Yuan was dismissed, Yu was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 人物時望，素不為眾所稱，及當樞務，聲問頓減。

translations.literal: His personal character and contemporary reputation had never been praised by the multitude; when he took charge of pivotal affairs, his renown abruptly declined.
translations.idiomatic: His character and standing had never won much public esteem, and once he assumed control of state affairs, his reputation fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 玙又奏置太一神壇於南郊之東，請上躬行祀事。

translations.literal: Yu again memorialized to establish an altar to the Great Unity Spirit east of the southern suburb, requesting that the sovereign personally perform the sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yu further memorialized for an altar to the spirit of the Great Unity to be built east of the southern suburban sacrifice ground, and asked that the emperor perform the rites in person.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘗不豫，太卜云：「崇在山川。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong once fell ill; the Grand Diviner said: 'Reverence lies in mountains and rivers.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong once fell ill, the Grand Diviner declared, "The remedy lies in honoring the mountains and rivers."

sentences.zh: 」玙乃遣女巫分行天下，祈祭名山大川。

translations.literal: Yu then dispatched shamannesses to travel throughout the realm, praying and sacrificing at famous mountains and great rivers.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis Yu sent shamannesses throughout the empire to offer prayers and sacrifices at renowned mountains and major rivers.

sentences.zh: 巫皆盛服乘傳而行，上令中使監之，因緣為奸，所至干托長吏，以邀賂遺。

translations.literal: The shamannesses all traveled in splendid dress by relay post; the emperor ordered palace envoys to supervise them, who took the opportunity to commit wrongdoing, everywhere importuning local chief officials to solicit bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The shamannesses traveled in lavish dress by imperial relay, while palace envoys were ordered to supervise them. These envoys used their position to commit abuses, importuning local officials wherever they went to extract bribes and gifts.

sentences.zh: 一巫盛年而美，以惡少年數十自隨，尤為蠹弊，與其徒宿於黃州傳舍。

translations.literal: One shamanness, in the prime of life and beautiful, took several tens of wicked youths with her; she was especially corrupt, and she and her followers lodged at the relay station in Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: One shamanness, young and beautiful, was accompanied by several dozen rowdy youths. Her party was especially notorious for corruption. She and her followers lodged at the relay station in Huang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 刺史左震晨至，驛門扃鐍，不可啟，震破鎖而入，曳女巫階下斬之，所從惡少年皆斃。

translations.literal: Prefect Zuo Zhen arrived in the morning; the relay gate was bolted and could not be opened. Zhen broke the lock and entered, dragged the shamanness down the steps and beheaded her, and all the wicked youths who followed were killed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the prefect, Zuo Zhen, arrived to find the relay station gate bolted shut. He broke the lock, entered, dragged the shamanness down the steps and beheaded her, and had all her rowdy followers put to death.

sentences.zh: 閱其贓賂數十萬，震籍以上聞，仍請贓錢代貧民租稅，其中使發遣歸京，肅宗不能詰。

translations.literal: Examining her bribes, they amounted to several hundred thousand; Zhen registered them and reported upward, and further requested that the illicit money substitute for poor people's rent and tax. The palace envoy was sent back to the capital; Emperor Suzong could not interrogate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He found bribes amounting to several hundred thousand cash. Zhen inventoried the goods and reported to the throne, requesting that the confiscated funds be applied to poor people's rent and tax obligations. The supervising palace envoy was sent back to the capital, and Emperor Suzong was unable to pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 肅宗親謁九宮神，慇勤於祠禱，皆玙所啟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong personally visited the Nine Palaces Spirit, being earnest in sacrificial prayer—all was initiated by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's personal visits to the Nine Palaces deity and his zealous devotion to prayer and sacrifice were all instigated by Yu.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，罷知政事，為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was removed from managing state affairs and made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he was removed from the chancellorship and appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，兼揚州長史、御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, he was concurrently made Chief Administrator of Yang Prefecture and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2 (761) he was concurrently appointed Chief Administrator of Yangzhou and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 兗淮南節度使。

translations.literal: And appointed Huainan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Military Commissioner of the Huainan circuit.

sentences.zh: 肅宗南郊禮畢，以玙使持節都督越州諸軍事、越州刺史，充浙江東道節度觀察處置使，本官兼御史大夫，祠祭使如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong completed the southern suburban rites, Yu was made envoy holding credentials, Area Commander of all military affairs of Yue Prefecture and Prefect of Yue, and appointed Military Commissioner and Observation and Disposition Commissioner of the Zhejiang Eastern Circuit; his original offices including Censor-in-Chief continued, and his role as Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong completed the southern suburban sacrifice, Yu was commissioned as Area Commander of Yue and Prefect of Yue, with appointment as Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of the Zhejiang Eastern Circuit. He retained his rank as Censor-in-Chief and continued as Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites.

sentences.zh: 入為太子少保，轉少師。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, then was transferred to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and later transferred to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 大曆三年六月卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Dali he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of Dali 3 (768).

sentences.zh: 玙以祭祀妖妄致位將相，時以左道進者，往往有之。

translations.literal: Yu, through heterodox and delusive sacrificial rites, attained the rank of general and chancellor; at the time those who advanced by heterodox ways were often to be found.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had risen to the rank of general and chancellor through delusive sacrificial practices, and in that era many others advanced by similar heterodox means.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年八月，道士李國禎以道術見，因奏皇室仙系，宜修崇靈跡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Guangde, the Daoist Li Guozhen was received for his Daoist arts; he thereupon memorialized that the imperial house's immortal lineage should have its numinous traces repaired and honored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Guangde 2 (764), the Daoist Li Guozhen was received at court for his occult arts. He memorialized that the imperial clan's immortal lineage ought to have its sacred sites restored and venerated.

sentences.zh: 請於昭應縣南三十里山頂置天華上宮露台、大地婆父、三皇、道君、太古天皇、中古伏羲媧皇等祠堂，並置掃灑宮戶一百戶。

translations.literal: He requested that on the mountaintop thirty li south of Zhaoying County be established the Heavenly Flower Upper Palace terrace, halls to the Great Earth Matron-Father, the Three Sovereigns, the Daoist Lord, the Primordial Heavenly Sovereign, the Middle-Ancient Fuxi and Nuwa Sovereigns, and other shrines, and that one hundred households for sweeping and maintenance be established.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that shrines be built on a mountaintop thirty li south of Zhaoying County—including the Heavenly Flower Upper Palace terrace, the Great Earth Matron-Father, the Three Sovereigns, the Daoist Lord, the Primordial Heavenly Sovereign, and the Middle-Ancient Fuxi and Nüwa—and that one hundred households be assigned to maintain them.

sentences.zh: 又於縣之東義扶谷故湫置龍堂，並許之。

translations.literal: He further requested establishment of a Dragon Hall at the old pool in Yifu Valley east of the county, and all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that a Dragon Hall be built at the old sacred pool in Yifu Valley east of the county, and all of these requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑荒，人甚不安，昭應縣令梁鎮上表曰：

translations.literal: At the time there was famine; the people were greatly unsettled. The Magistrate of Zhaoying County, Liang Zhen, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the land and the people were deeply distressed. Liang Zhen, magistrate of Zhaoying County, submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國以人為本，害其本則非國；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the state takes the people as its foundation; to harm that foundation is not to be a state;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a state rests upon its people as its foundation; to harm that foundation is to cease being a state;

sentences.zh: 神以人為主，虐其主則非神。

translations.literal: spirits take people as their masters; to mistreat those masters is not to be a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: and that spirits take human beings as their masters— to abuse those masters is to cease being worthy of worship as a spirit.

sentences.zh: 故昔之聖王，所以極陳理道，明著祀典，將愛其人而慎用其財力，敬其神而虔恭於祠祭。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of old, for this reason fully expounded the Way, clearly set forth the sacrificial canon, intending to cherish their people and carefully use their wealth and labor, to revere their spirits and be devout and reverent in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the sage kings of antiquity expounded the Way at length and made the sacrificial canon explicit: they cherished their people and used wealth and labor sparingly, while revering the spirits through sincere and measured worship.

sentences.zh: 故神享其明德而降之福，人受其大賚而盡其力，然後神人以和，而國家可保也。

translations.literal: Thus spirits enjoyed their bright virtue and bestowed blessings; people received their great bounty and exerted their strength—only then did spirits and people harmonize, and the state could be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When spirits delighted in the rulers' luminous virtue and sent down blessings, and the people received the state's bounty and gave their full effort, then spirits and people were in harmony and the state could endure.

sentences.zh: 一昨蟊賊作孽，水旱為災，雖王畿皆遍，而臣縣最苦。

translations.literal: Recently rebels wrought havoc and flood and drought became disasters; though the capital region was everywhere affected, your subject's county suffered most bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Only recently rebels ravaged the land and flood and drought brought disaster. Though suffering was widespread even in the capital region, your subject's county has borne the worst of it.

sentences.zh: 此則神之不能御大災明矣，又何力於陛下而得列祀典哉！

translations.literal: This then makes clear that spirits cannot ward off great disasters—what power have they toward Your Majesty that they should be entered in the sacrificial canon!
translations.idiomatic: This plainly shows that the spirits cannot avert great calamities. What power do they possess, that Your Majesty should enroll them in the state sacrificial canon?

sentences.zh: 用以殘弊之餘，當凶荒之歲，丁壯素出家入仕，羸老方飛芻輓粟，令但供億王事，已不堪命，更奔走鬼道，何以聊生？

translations.literal: To use what remains of the exhausted and broken, in years of famine and disaster—able-bodied men have long since left home for office, the weak and old are just now hauling fodder and grain—ordered only to supply the king's affairs, already unable to bear the burden, yet further driven to run the ghostly Way: how may they make a living?
translations.idiomatic: To impose new burdens on a people already broken, in years of famine and disaster—when able-bodied men have long since left for government service and the weak and elderly are barely able to haul fodder and grain—when they can scarcely meet the demands of state service, how can they also be driven to serve these ghostly cults and still find a way to live?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞天地之神，尊之極者，掃地可祭，精意可饗。

translations.literal: Your subject further has heard that for spirits of Heaven and Earth, those most honored may be sacrificed to with swept ground; with refined intent they may be feasted.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the highest spirits of Heaven and Earth may be worshipped with no more than swept ground and offered sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦何必廢先王之典，崇俗巫之說，走南畝之客，殺東鄰之牛，而後冀非妄之福。

translations.literal: Why must Your Majesty abandon the canons of the former kings, exalt vulgar shaman teachings, drive away the guests of the southern fields, kill the eastern neighbor's ox, and only then hope for non-delusive blessing?
translations.idiomatic: Why must Your Majesty abandon the rites of the ancient kings, elevate vulgar shamanistic teachings, drive the farmers from their fields, slaughter the neighbor's ox—as in the proverb—and only then hope for blessings that are not illusory?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲為人祈福，福未至而人已困矣！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty wishes to seek blessing for the people, before blessing arrives the people are already distressed!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty wishes to seek blessings for the people, before any blessing arrives the people are already exhausted!

sentences.zh: 其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason the project must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 陛下不視昔者有道之君，至德之後，曷不卑宮室，惡飲食，恭己以遂萬物之性哉！

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty not observe the rulers of old who possessed the Way, the heirs of supreme virtue—how they did not lower their palaces, abhorred lavish food and drink, and with reverent self-restraint followed the nature of the myriad things!
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty not observed how the sage rulers of old, heirs of supreme virtue, kept their palaces modest, their fare simple, and governed with reverent restraint so that all things might follow their natural course?

sentences.zh: 陛下今違神亭育之心，竭人疲睏之力，如是又何從而致其福哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty now violates the spirit of Heaven's nourishing care, exhausts the people's weary and exhausted strength—how then may blessing be attained?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now violates Heaven's nurturing purpose and exhausts a people already worn down with toil. How, then, can blessing possibly be attained?

sentences.zh: 此又不可二也。

translations.literal: This is again the second reason it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason it must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 又陛下宗廟之敬極矣，尚無一月三祭之禮；

translations.literal: Further, Your Majesty's reverence for the ancestral temple is already extreme, yet there is still no rite of three sacrifices in one month;
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, Your Majesty's reverence for the ancestral temple is already beyond compare, yet even there the rites do not require three sacrifices in a single month;

sentences.zh: 今此獨為，則宗廟之靈，將等以親疏，校以厚薄，陛下又何以言哉？

translations.literal: if this alone is done, then the spirits of the ancestral temple will be ranked by closeness and distance, compared by lavishness and meagerness—what may Your Majesty say to that?
translations.idiomatic: yet for these new shrines alone such extraordinary devotion is proposed. Will not the spirits of the ancestral temple be ranked by degrees of kinship and measured by degrees of lavishness? What account can Your Majesty give of that?

sentences.zh: 此又不可三也。

translations.literal: This is again the third reason it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason it must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 又大地婆父，祀典無文，言甚不經，義無可取。

translations.literal: Further, the Great Earth Matron-Father has no entry in the sacrificial canon; the name is very uncanonical and the principle nothing to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the 'Great Earth Matron-Father' has no place in the sacrificial canon. The title is utterly uncanonical and offers no valid principle to follow.

sentences.zh: 若陛下待與大地建祖宗之廟，必上天貽向背之責，陛下又何以為詞哉？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty intends to build an ancestral temple for the Great Earth alongside it, Heaven will surely impose blame for favor and disfavor—what words will Your Majesty have?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty intends to build an ancestral temple for the Great Earth, Heaven will surely hold you accountable for confusing proper order. What defense could Your Majesty offer?

sentences.zh: 此又不可四也。

translations.literal: This is again the fourth reason it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason it must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 夫湫者，龍之所居也。

translations.literal: Now a pool is where dragons dwell.
translations.idiomatic: A sacred pool is where dragons dwell.

sentences.zh: 龍得水則神，無水則螻蟻之匹也。

translations.literal: When dragons obtain water they are numinous; without water they are the equal of ants.
translations.idiomatic: When dragons have water they are divine; without water they are no more than ants.

sentences.zh: 故知水存則龍在，水竭則龍亡，此愚智之所同知矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows: when water exists the dragon is present; when water is exhausted the dragon perishes—this the foolish and wise alike know.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when water remains, the dragon remains; when the water dries up, the dragon is gone. This is understood alike by the wise and the simple.

sentences.zh: 今湫竭已久，龍安所存？

translations.literal: Now the pool has long been dry—where can the dragon abide?
translations.idiomatic: The pool has long since dried up. Where, then, can the dragon still dwell?

sentences.zh: 陛下又崇飾祠宇，豐潔薦奠，為去龍之穴，破生人之產，人且怨矣，神何歆哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty further lavishly adorns the shrine halls and richly provides offerings, removing the dragon's lair and destroying the living people's livelihood—the people will resent it; how would spirits delight!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty would lavishly adorn shrine halls and offer rich sacrifices—destroying what was once the dragon's dwelling and ruining the livelihood of the living people. The people will resent this; how could any spirit accept such offerings with pleasure?

sentences.zh: 此又不可五也。

translations.literal: This is again the fifth reason it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth reason it must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 其道君、三皇、五帝，則兩京及所都之處，皆建宮觀祠廟，時設齋醮饗祀，國有彝典，官有常禮，蓋無闕失，何勞神役靈？

translations.literal: As for the Daoist Lord, the Three Sovereigns, and the Five Emperors—in both capitals and wherever the court is established, palace halls, temples, and shrines are all built, and fasting and sacrificial feasts are regularly set; the state has constant canons, officials have regular rites—there is essentially no deficiency; why trouble spirits and command numinous powers?
translations.idiomatic: As for the Daoist Lord, the Three Sovereigns, and the Five Emperors—in both capitals and wherever the court resides, monasteries, temples, and shrines have already been built, with regular fasting rites and sacrifices. The state has its established canon and officials their regular observances. Nothing is lacking. Why must spirits be summoned and numinous powers conscripted anew?

sentences.zh: 此又不可六也。

translations.literal: This is again the sixth reason it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth reason it must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 臣稽先王之典禮，觀前聖之軌躅，休咎豐凶，災祥禍福，必主帝王五事，不在山川百神。

translations.literal: Your subject has examined the former kings' ritual canon and observed the former sages' footprints: fortune and misfortune, abundance and disaster, auspicious and inauspicious signs, blessing and calamity—all surely depend on the five affairs of the emperor, not on the hundred spirits of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined the ritual canon of the ancient kings and traced the path of the sage rulers of old: whether the times bring fortune or misfortune, abundance or disaster, auspicious signs or calamity—all depend on the five duties of the sovereign, not on the hundred spirits of mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 此又不可七也。

translations.literal: This is again the seventh reason it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh reason it must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 臣伏察此弊，頗知其由。

translations.literal: Your subject, bowing, has examined this abuse and knows its cause rather well.
translations.idiomatic: Having examined this abuse closely, I believe I understand its cause.

sentences.zh: 蓋以道士李國禎等動眾則得人，興工則獲利，祭祀則受胙，主執則弄權。

translations.literal: It is because Daoists such as Li Guozhen, when they mobilize the multitude, thereby gain followers; when they raise works, they obtain profit; when sacrifices are performed, they receive sacrificial meat; when they preside, they manipulate power.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Li Guozhen and his like gain followers whenever they mobilize the people, profit whenever they launch construction, receive sacrificial offerings whenever rites are performed, and wield power whenever they take charge.

sentences.zh: 是以鼓動禁中，熒惑天聽，踰越險阻，負荷粢盛，以日系年，無時而息。

translations.literal: Therefore they stir up the inner palace, dazzle Heaven's hearing, cross dangerous passes, bear sacrificial grain—day by day, year by year, without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they stir up activity within the palace, mislead the imperial ear, cross dangerous terrain, and burden the people with sacrificial supplies—day after day, year after year, without respite.

sentences.zh: 曾不謂神功力，空止竭人膏血，以使人神胥怨，災孽並生。

translations.literal: They never speak of the spirits' divine power, but only exhaust the people's lifeblood, so that people and spirits alike resent, and disasters and calamities arise together.
translations.idiomatic: They never speak of the spirits' divine power, but only drain the people's lifeblood, until people and spirits alike are resentful and disasters multiply.

sentences.zh: 罔上害人，左道亂政，原情定罪，非殺而何！

translations.literal: Deceiving superiors and harming the people, heterodox ways disordering government—examining the circumstances to fix guilt, if not execution, then what!
translations.idiomatic: They deceive the throne, harm the people, and use heterodox practices to corrupt government. Judging by the facts of the case, what punishment could they deserve but death?

sentences.zh: 臣昨受命之時，親承聖旨，務存安緝，許逐權宜。

translations.literal: When your subject yesterday received his commission, he personally received the sacred decree: strive to preserve peace and order, and was permitted to follow expedients.
translations.idiomatic: When I received my appointment yesterday, I was personally charged by Your Majesty to preserve peace and order, with permission to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 誠願沉鄴縣之巫，安流弊之俗，其所興兩祠土木之功、丹青之役、三六之祭、灑掃之戶，謹明宣旨，並以權宜停訖。

translations.literal: I sincerely wish to sink the shamans of Ye County and settle the corrupt customs; the two shrines' earth-and-wood works, cinnabar-and-green labors, the three-six sacrifices, and the sweeping households—I respectfully announced the imperial decree and, by expedient authority, halted them all.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly wished to suppress the shamans as at Ye County and restore a corrupted custom to order. I therefore announced Your Majesty's decree and, acting on my discretionary authority, halted all construction on the two shrines, the painting work, the thrice-daily sacrifices, and the maintenance households.

sentences.zh: 人吏百姓等，知陛下以從善為心，嫉惡為務，蠲除不急，劃革煩苛，皆喧呼於庭，抃躍於路，所徵糧糗，無不樂輸。

translations.literal: Officials, clerks, common people, and others, knowing Your Majesty takes following goodness as heart and hating evil as task, removing what is not urgent and cutting away what is vexatious—all shouted in the courtyards and danced in the roads; whatever grain and provisions were levied, none failed to give gladly.
translations.idiomatic: When officials and common people learned that Your Majesty's heart is set on following what is good and rooting out what is evil, and that unnecessary burdens were being lifted and oppressive regulations cut away, they shouted for joy in the courtyards and danced in the streets. Whatever grain and provisions were levied, they gave gladly.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以國禎等並交結中貴，狡蠹成性，臣雖忘身許國，不懼讒構，終恐賄及豪右，復為奸惡。

translations.literal: Your subject submits that Guozhen and the others all associate with palace favorites; craft and corruption are their nature. Though your subject forgets self in serving the state and does not fear slander, he ultimately fears bribes reaching powerful families and again becoming wicked.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Guozhen and his associates are allied with powerful eunuchs at court and are crafty and corrupt by nature. Though I am willing to risk myself in the state's service and do not fear slander, I fear that bribes will reach powerful families and that these men will again commit outrages.

sentences.zh: 其國禎等見據狀推勘，如獲贓狀，伏望許臣徵收，便充當縣郵館本用。

translations.literal: As for Guozhen and the others, according to the present evidence investigated, it is as if stolen goods were obtained; your subject bows and hopes Your Majesty will permit him to confiscate them and apply them to the county relay station's original uses.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation of Guozhen and his associates on the basis of the evidence already obtained has produced proof equivalent to a conviction for corruption. I respectfully ask permission to confiscate their assets and apply them to the county relay station's operating expenses.

sentences.zh: 其湫既竭，不可更置祠堂，又不當為大地建立祖廟，臣並請停。

translations.literal: The pool being already dry, no shrine hall may be further established; nor is it proper to build an ancestral temple for the Great Earth—your subject requests cessation of both.
translations.idiomatic: Since the pool has dried up, no shrine should be built there, and it is improper to erect an ancestral temple to the Great Earth. I request that both projects be halted.

sentences.zh: 其三皇、道君、天皇、伏羲、女媧等，既先各有宮廟，望請並於本所依禮齋祭。

translations.literal: As for the Three Sovereigns, Daoist Lord, Heavenly Sovereign, Fuxi, Nüwa, and the like—since each already has palace halls and temples, your subject hopes they may all be reverently sacrificed to at their original sites according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Three Sovereigns, the Daoist Lord, the Heavenly Sovereign, Fuxi, Nüwa, and the like—since each already has established shrines, I ask that sacrifices be performed at those original sites according to proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 李泌，字長源，其先遼東襄平人，西魏太保、八柱國司徒徒何弼之六代孫。

translations.literal: Li Bi, style name Changyuan, his ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong, sixth-generation descendant of Tuohe Bi, Grand Guardian and one of the Eight Pillars, Minister of Education of Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, courtesy name Changyuan, was descended from families of Xiangping in Liaodong. He was the sixth-generation descendant of Tuohe Bi, Grand Guardian and one of the Eight Pillars, Minister of Education of Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 今居京兆吳房令承休之子。

translations.literal: Now residing in Jingzhao, he was son of Magistrate Chengxiu of Wufang County.
translations.idiomatic: His family now lived in the Jingzhao region. He was the son of Li Chengxiu, magistrate of Wufang County.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，博涉經史，精究《易象》，善屬文，尤工於詩，以王佐自負。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, broadly traversed the classics and histories, deeply investigated the Images of the Changes, was skilled at literary composition, especially accomplished in poetry, and prided himself on being a king's assistant.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was exceptionally intelligent. He read widely in the classics and histories, mastered the imagery of the Book of Changes, wrote well, and was especially accomplished in poetry. He considered himself destined to serve as a king's chief minister.

sentences.zh: 張九齡、韋虛心、張廷珪皆器重之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling, Wei Xuxin, and Zhang Tinggui all greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, Wei Xuxin, and Zhang Tinggui all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 泌操尚不羈，恥隨常格仕進。

translations.literal: Bi's conduct and aims were unrestrained; he was ashamed to follow the usual pattern of advancement through office.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's temperament was free and unconventional, and he was reluctant to advance through the usual channels of official career.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，自嵩山上書論當世務，玄宗召見，令侍詔翰林，仍東宮供奉。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, from Mount Song he submitted a memorial discussing affairs of the age; Emperor Xuanzong summoned him for audience, ordered him to attend as Hanlin Drafting Attendant, and he also served the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he submitted a memorial from Mount Song discussing affairs of state. Emperor Xuanzong summoned him to court, appointed him Hanlin Drafting Attendant, and assigned him to serve the crown prince as well.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠忌其才辯，奏泌嘗為《感遇詩》，諷刺時政，詔於蘄春郡安置，乃潛遁名山，以習隱自適。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong resented his talent and eloquence, memorialized that Bi had once written 'Poems on Encountering Fate,' satirizing current politics; an edict ordered him settled in Qichun Prefecture. He then secretly fled to famous mountains, practicing reclusion for his own contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, jealous of his talent and eloquence, memorialized that Bi had written Poems on Encountering Fate, which satirized current politics. An edict ordered him sent to Qichun Prefecture for resettlement. Bi instead went into hiding on famous mountains, devoting himself to the life of a recluse.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，祿山構難，肅宗北巡，至靈武即位，遣使訪召。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, Lushan raised rebellion; Emperor Suzong toured north, ascended the throne at Lingwu, and dispatched envoys to seek and summon him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao reign An Lushan rebelled. Emperor Suzong withdrew northward, took the throne at Lingwu, and sent envoys to seek him out.

sentences.zh: 會泌自嵩、潁間冒難奔赴行在，至彭原郡謁見，陳古今成敗之機，甚稱旨，延致臥內，動皆顧問。

translations.literal: It happened that Bi, from between Song and Ying, braved hardship to hurry to the mobile court; arriving at Pengyuan Prefecture he had audience, expounded the mechanisms of success and failure in ancient and modern times, greatly matched the emperor's intent, was received within the sleeping quarters, and in every movement was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Bi happened to be traveling between Mount Song and the Ying region and braved hardship to reach the mobile court. He had audience at Pengyuan Prefecture and expounded the patterns of success and failure through history. The emperor was greatly pleased, received him in his private quarters, and consulted him on nearly every matter.

sentences.zh: 泌稱山人，固辭官秩，特以散官寵之，解褐拜銀青光祿大夫，俾掌樞務。

translations.literal: Bi styled himself Mountain Man and firmly declined official rank; he was specially favored with a scattered office, and upon leaving the cloth was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and entrusted to manage pivotal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bi styled himself the Mountain Man and firmly declined regular office. The emperor honored him with a special appointment, conferring upon him the rank of Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness while entrusting him with affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 至於四言文狀、將相遷除，皆與泌參議，權逾宰相，仍判元帥廣平王軍司馬事。

translations.literal: As for four-character documents and memorials, and the promotion and removal of generals and chancellors—all were deliberated with Bi; his power exceeded the Chancellor's, and he still served as acting Army Vice-Marshal for the Prince of Guangping, the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials in four-character prose and the appointment and dismissal of generals and chancellors were all discussed with Bi. His authority exceeded that of the chancellor, and he also served as acting Army Vice-Marshal on the staff of the Prince of Guangping, commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 肅宗每謂曰：「卿當上皇天寶中，為朕師友，下判廣平行軍，朕父子三人，資卿道義。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong often said to him: 'You, sir, in the Tianbao era of the Retired Emperor, were teacher and friend to me; below you judge the Guangping army on campaign—we father and two sons, three men, rely on your moral guidance.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong often told him, "In the Tianbao era you were teacher and friend to me when I was crown prince. Now you serve on the Guangping army's campaign staff. We three—father and two sons—depend on your moral guidance."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he valued.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 尋為中書令崔圓、幸臣李輔國害其能，將有不利於泌。

translations.literal: Before long, Chief Minister Cui Yuan and the favored minister Li Fuguo, resenting his ability, were about to act harmfully toward Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chief Minister Cui Yuan and the favored minister Li Fuguo, jealous of his ability, were plotting against him.

sentences.zh: 泌懼，乞游衡山，優詔許之，給以三品祿俸，遂隱衡岳，絕粒棲神。

translations.literal: Bi feared this, requested to travel to Mount Heng, and a gracious edict permitted it, granting third-rank salary; he then hid on Mount Heng, abstaining from grain and dwelling in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, fearing for his safety, asked permission to retire to Mount Heng. A gracious edict granted his request and provided him third-rank salary. He then lived in seclusion on Mount Heng, practicing grain abstention and spiritual cultivation.

sentences.zh: 興元初，征赴行在，遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan, he was summoned to the mobile court and promoted to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xingyuan era he was summoned to the mobile court and appointed Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，除陝州長史，充陝、虢都防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, he was made Chief Administrator of Shan Prefecture and appointed Metropolitan Defense and Observation Commissioner of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 (785) he was appointed Chief Administrator of Shanzhou and Metropolitan Defense and Observation Commissioner of Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，泌奏：「虢州盧氏山冶，近出瑟瑟，請充獻，禁人開採。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, Bi memorialized: 'The smelting works at Mount Lushi in Guo Prefecture have recently produced sese gems; your subject requests they be submitted as tribute and that people be forbidden to mine them.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhenyuan 2, Bi memorialized: "The smelting works at Mount Lushi in Guo Prefecture have recently yielded sese gems. I request that they be submitted as tribute and that private mining be prohibited."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「瑟瑟之寶，中土所無今產於近甸，實為靈貺。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Sese gems are treasures the central land does not have; now produced in the nearby fields, this is truly a numinous bestowal.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Sese gems are treasures that the central plains have never possessed. That they now appear in a nearby district is truly a numinous gift from Heaven."

sentences.zh: 朕不飾器玩，不尚珍奇，常思返朴之風，用明躬儉之節。

translations.literal: We do not adorn vessels and curios, do not esteem rare wonders, constantly think of returning to simplicity's wind, and use this to display personal frugality's measure.
translations.idiomatic: We do not adorn ourselves with luxuries or prize rare curiosities. We constantly aspire to the spirit of simplicity and seek to exemplify personal frugality.

sentences.zh: 其出瑟瑟之處，任百姓求采，不宜禁止。

translations.literal: Where sese is produced, let the common people seek and mine as they wish; it is not fitting to forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Where the sese gems are found, let the people mine them freely. They should not be prohibited.

sentences.zh: 」就加泌檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bi was additionally made Acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Bi was appointed Acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時陳、許戍邊卒三千自京西逃歸，至州境，泌潛師險隘，左右攻擊，盡誅之。

translations.literal: At the time three thousand border-garrison soldiers of Chen and Xu, fleeing from west of the capital, returned; reaching the prefectural border, Bi secretly deployed troops at narrow passes, attacked from both sides, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time three thousand border garrison troops from Chen and Xu who had deserted from west of the capital were returning home. When they reached his jurisdiction, Bi secretly deployed troops at narrow passes, attacked them from both flanks, and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 尋拜中書侍郎、平章事、集賢崇文館學士、修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Hall of Venerated Literature, and Compiler of National History.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Hall of Venerated Literature, and Compiler of National History.

sentences.zh: 初，張延賞大減官員，人情咨怨，泌請復之，以從人欲，因是奏罷兼試額內佔闕等官，加百官俸料，隨閒劇加置手力課，上從之，人人以為便。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Yanshang had greatly reduced officials; popular sentiment murmured in resentment. Bi requested restoration to follow people's desires; thereby he memorialized to abolish concurrent examination quota and vacancy-occupying offices, increase all officials' salary provisions, and according to busyness or leisure add labor-service levies— the emperor followed this, and everyone considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Yanshang had drastically reduced the number of officials, provoking widespread resentment. Bi requested that the reductions be reversed to satisfy popular sentiment. He also memorialized to abolish certain concurrent examination and vacancy-filling posts, increase officials' salaries, and add labor-service allowances according to the demands of each post. The emperor approved, and everyone regarded the changes as beneficial.

sentences.zh: 而竇參旁奏，遂改易，使同品之內，月俸多少累等。

translations.literal: But Dou Can submitted a side memorial and thereby altered it, so that within the same rank monthly salary had many graduated grades.
translations.idiomatic: But Dou Can submitted a competing memorial that altered the plan, creating multiple graduated salary levels even within the same official rank.

sentences.zh: 泌又奏請罷拾遺、補闕，上雖不從，亦不授人，故諫司惟韓皋、歸登而已。

translations.literal: Bi again memorialized requesting the abolition of the Gatherers of Omissions and Supplemental Remonstrance posts; although the emperor did not agree, he also did not appoint anyone, so in the Remonstrance Bureau there were only Han Gao and Gui Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi again petitioned to abolish the posts of Remonstrance and Supplemental Remonstrance Adviser. The emperor declined, yet appointed no one to fill them, so the Remonstrance Bureau held only Han Gao and Gui Deng.

sentences.zh: 泌仍命收其署湌錢，令登等寓食於中書舍人，故時戲云：「韓諫議雖分左右，歸拾遺莫辨存亡。

translations.literal: Bi still ordered the collection of their office stipend money and had Deng and the others lodge and eat with the Secretariat Drafters; hence people jestingly said: "Though Remonstrance Adviser Han divides left and right, Returning Remonstrance cannot distinguish life from death."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi also ordered their office stipends seized and had Deng and his colleagues board with the Secretariat drafters. People then quipped: "Remonstrance Adviser Han may stand left or right, but when it comes to Returning Remonstrance, none can tell whether he lives or dies."

sentences.zh: 」如是者三年。

translations.literal: " Thus it continued for three years.
translations.idiomatic: This went on for three years.

sentences.zh: 至貞元五年，以前東都防禦判官、殿中侍御史、內供奉韋綬為左補闕，監察御史梁肅右補闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, Wei Shou, former Eastern Capital Defense staff officer, Palace Attendant Censor, and Inner Attendant, was made Left Supplemental Remonstrance Adviser, and Supervising Censor Liang Su Right Supplemental Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhenyuan era, Wei Shou—formerly staff officer for Eastern Capital defense, Palace Attendant Censor, and Inner Attendant—was appointed Left Supplemental Remonstrance Adviser, and Supervising Censor Liang Su was appointed to the right.

sentences.zh: 既復置，人心忻然。

translations.literal: Once the posts were restored, people's hearts rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When the posts were restored, public sentiment brightened.

sentences.zh: 順宗在春宮，妃蕭氏母郜國公主交通外人，上疑其有他，連坐貶黜者數人，皇儲亦危。

translations.literal: When Shunzong was in the Eastern Palace, the mother of his consort Lady Xiao, the Princess of Guo State, had dealings with outsiders; the emperor suspected ulterior motives, several were implicated and demoted, and the crown prince's position was also imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shunzong was crown prince, the mother of his consort Lady Xiao—the Princess of Guo—was found to have improper contact with outsiders. The emperor suspected deeper intrigue; several people were implicated and banished, and even the heir apparent's position hung in peril.

sentences.zh: 泌百端奏說，上意方解。

translations.literal: Bi memorialized in every possible way to persuade him, and only then did the emperor's mind ease.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi pleaded his case from every angle in memorial after memorial, until at last the emperor's suspicions lifted.

sentences.zh: 泌頗有讜直之風，而談神仙詭道，或云嘗與赤松子、王喬、安期、羨門游處，故為代所輕，雖詭道求容，不為時君所重。

translations.literal: Bi had quite a reputation for forthright remonstrance, yet he spoke of immortals and occult doctrines, and some said he had once consorted with Chisongzi, Wang Qiao, Anqi, and Xianmen; therefore his age looked down on him, and though he used occult ways to win favor, he was not truly valued by the reigning sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi bore a reputation for blunt integrity, yet he also trafficked in immortals and esoteric lore—some even claimed he had kept company with Chisongzi, Wang Qiao, Anqi, and Xianmen. His contemporaries therefore held him lightly; though he courted favor through occult arts, the reigning emperor never truly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 德宗初即位，尤惡巫祝怪誕之士。

translations.literal: When Dezong first ascended the throne, he especially loathed shamans, prayer masters, and practitioners of freakish doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong first took the throne, he especially despised shamans, prayer masters, and purveyors of outlandish superstition.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗重陰陽祠祝之說，用妖人王玙為宰相，或命巫媼乘驛行郡縣以為厭勝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Suzong had valued yin-yang rites and prayer, employed the sorcerer Wang Yu as chancellor, and sometimes ordered shaman women to travel by post-horse through commanderies and counties for apotropaic rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong, yin-yang ritualism and prayer had held sway: the sorcerer Wang Yu was made chancellor, and shamanesses were sometimes dispatched by courier post through the provinces to perform rites of warding and suppression.

sentences.zh: 凡有所興造功役，動牽禁忌。

translations.literal: Whenever there was construction or public works, every move was bound by taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Every public work and construction project was shackled to ritual taboos.

sentences.zh: 而黎干用左道位至尹京，嘗內集眾工，編刺珠繡為御衣，既成而焚之，以為禳禬，且無虛月。

translations.literal: Li Gan, by heterodox arts, rose to the position of capital intendant; he once gathered artisans within the palace to weave and embroider pearl-studded imperial robes, and once finished burned them as ritual expiation—not a month went without it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan had risen to govern the capital through heterodox arts. He once assembled artisans inside the palace to weave and embroider pearl-studded imperial robes, then burned them upon completion as rites of expiation—month after month without pause.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮，頗知其事，即位之後，罷集僧於內道場，除巫祝之祀。

translations.literal: Dezong, while in the Eastern Palace, knew these matters quite well; after ascending the throne, he abolished the gathering of monks in the inner oratory and eliminated shamanistic rites.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince, Dezong had seen these abuses clearly. Once enthroned, he ended the assembly of monks in the inner oratory and swept away shamanistic worship.

sentences.zh: 有司言宣政內廊壞，請修繕。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported that the inner corridor of Xuanzheng Hall was damaged and requested repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported damage to the inner corridor of the Xuanzheng Hall and petitioned for repairs.

sentences.zh: 而太卜云：「孟冬為魁岡，不利穿築，請卜他月。

translations.literal: But the Grand Diviner said: "The first month of winter is Kui Gang; excavation and construction are inauspicious—please choose another month by divination."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Diviner objected: "The first month of winter falls under Kui Gang—a geomantic taboo against digging and building. Please choose another month by divination."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「《春秋》之義，啟塞從時，何魁岡之有？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that opening and closing passages follow the season—what of Kui Gang?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that passages should be opened or closed according to the season—what relevance has Kui Gang?"

sentences.zh: 」卒命修之。

translations.literal: " He finally ordered the repairs.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the work to proceed.

sentences.zh: 又代宗山陵靈駕發引，上號送於承天門，見辒辌不當道，稍指午未間。

translations.literal: Again, when the spirit carriage for Emperor Daizong's tomb departed, the emperor wailed in mourning at Chengtian Gate and saw the funeral carriage not on the proper route, veering slightly toward the noon and wei direction.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial funeral procession for Emperor Daizong's tomb set out, the emperor wailed in farewell at Chengtian Gate and noticed the spirit carriage had strayed from the direct route, angling toward the noon and wei hours.

sentences.zh: 問其故，有司對曰：「陛下本命在午，故不敢當道。

translations.literal: Asked the reason, the relevant offices replied: "Your Majesty's natal hour is at noon, so we dared not block the route."
translations.idiomatic: When he asked why, officials answered: "Your Majesty's natal hour falls at noon, so we dared not let the carriage cross your path."

sentences.zh: 」上號泣曰：「安有枉靈駕而謀身利。

translations.literal: " The emperor wailed and wept: "How can one bend the spirit carriage to seek personal advantage?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept aloud: "How can one bend the imperial spirit carriage to serve one's own fortune?"

sentences.zh: 」卒命直午而行。

translations.literal: " He finally ordered it to proceed straight at noon.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the procession to proceed straight through the noon hour.

sentences.zh: 及建中末，寇戎內梗，桑道茂有城奉天之說，上稍以時日禁忌為意，而雅聞泌長於鬼道，故自外征還，以至大用，時論不以為愜。

translations.literal: By the end of Jianzhong, invaders troubled the realm from within; Sang Daomao had a prophecy about fortifying Fengtian, and the emperor gradually grew mindful of calendrical taboos; he had long heard that Bi excelled in occult arts, so when recalled from outside to great employment, contemporary opinion did not find it satisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Jianzhong era, rebellion roiled the empire within. Sang Daomao's prophecy about fortifying Fengtian made the emperor increasingly heedful of calendrical taboos, and he had long heard that Li Bi excelled in occult arts. When Li Bi was summoned from exile to high office, contemporary opinion found the appointment ill-suited.

sentences.zh: 及在相位，隨時俯仰，無足可稱。

translations.literal: Once in the chancellorship, he adapted to circumstances without distinction worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the chancellorship, he merely bent with the times—nothing worth commending.

sentences.zh: 復引顧況輩輕薄之流，動為朝士戲侮，頗貽譏誚。

translations.literal: He also brought in frivolous figures like Gu Kuang, who were constantly mocked by court gentlemen, drawing considerable ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: He also promoted frivolous men such as Gu Kuang, who were constantly mocked by court gentlemen and brought him no little ridicule.

sentences.zh: 年六十八薨，贈太子太傅，賻禮有加。

translations.literal: At age sixty-eight he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with enhanced funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with funeral rites beyond the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 泌放曠敏辯，好大言，自出入中禁，累為權幸忌嫉恆由智免；

translations.literal: Bi was unrestrained, quick-witted, and fond of grand pronouncements; from his entry into the inner palace, those in power repeatedly envied and resented him, yet he always escaped harm through wit;
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi was free-spirited, sharp-tongued, and fond of bold pronouncements. From the day he entered the inner palace, the powerful envied and resented him again and again, yet he always slipped free through wit;

sentences.zh: 終以言論縱橫，上悟聖主，以躋相位。

translations.literal: ultimately through eloquent discourse he moved the sage sovereign and rose to the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: in the end his eloquence won over the sage sovereign and carried him to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十捲。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings filled twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子繁，少聰警，有才名，無行義。

translations.literal: His son Fan was clever and alert from youth, with a literary reputation but no moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Fan was clever from youth and won a name for talent, but lacked moral character.

sentences.zh: 泌為相，嘗引薦夏縣處士北平陽城為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Bi was chancellor, he once recommended Yang Cheng, a recluse of Xia County in Beiping, as Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Bi served as chancellor, he once recommended Yang Cheng, a recluse from Xia County in Beiping, for appointment as Remonstrance Adviser.

sentences.zh: 城道直，既遇知己，深德之。

translations.literal: Cheng was upright in conduct; having met a true patron, he deeply appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng was a man of upright character; having found a true patron, he held Li Bi in deep gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及泌歿，戶部尚書裴延齡巧佞奉上，德宗信任，竊弄威權，舉朝側目。

translations.literal: After Bi's death, Pei Yanling, Minister of Revenue, was artful and sycophantic toward the throne; Dezong trusted him, and he secretly wielded authority—the whole court looked on with sidelong eyes.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Bi's death, Pei Yanling, Minister of Revenue—a sycophantic schemer who flattered the throne—won Emperor Dezong's trust and secretly wielded power, arousing the whole court's resentment.

sentences.zh: 城中正之士，尤忿嫉之。

translations.literal: Cheng, a man of integrity, especially resented and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng, a man of integrity, hated him above all.

sentences.zh: 一日盡疏其過惡，欲密論奏，以繁故人子，為可親信，遂示其疏草，兼請繁繕寫。

translations.literal: One day he fully memorialized Yanling's wrongs and wished to submit a confidential memorial; considering Fan the son of an old friend and trustworthy, he showed him the draft and also asked Fan to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: One day Yang Cheng drafted a full catalogue of Pei Yanling's crimes, intending a confidential memorial. Because Li Fan was an old friend's son and seemed trustworthy, he showed him the draft and asked him to make a fair copy.

sentences.zh: 繁既寫，悉能記之，其夕乃徑詣延齡，具述其事。

translations.literal: After Fan had copied it, he memorized it entirely; that very evening he went straight to Yanling and recounted the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan copied it—and memorized every word. That very evening he went straight to Pei Yanling and told him everything.

sentences.zh: 延齡聞之，即時請對，盡以城章中欲論事件，一一先自解。

translations.literal: When Yanling heard this, he immediately requested audience and addressed each point Yang Cheng's memorial intended to raise, explaining them all in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling, hearing this, immediately sought audience with the emperor and preemptively addressed every charge Yang Cheng's memorial was meant to raise.

sentences.zh: 及城疏入，德宗以為妄，不之省。

translations.literal: When Cheng's memorial arrived, Dezong considered it reckless and did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Cheng's memorial arrived, Emperor Dezong dismissed it as reckless fabrication and paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 泌與右補闕、翰林學士梁肅友善，嘗命繁持所著文請肅潤色。

translations.literal: Bi was on friendly terms with Right Supplemental Remonstrance Adviser and Hanlin Academician Liang Su, and once had Fan bring his writings to Liang Su for polishing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi was close to Right Supplemental Remonstrance Adviser and Hanlin Academician Liang Su, and once sent Li Fan to bring his writings to Liang Su for polishing.

sentences.zh: 繁亦自有學術，肅待之甚厚，因許師事，日熟其門。

translations.literal: Fan also had learning of his own; Liang Su treated him very generously and permitted him to study as a disciple, visiting his house daily.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan had learning of his own; Liang Su treated him generously, accepted him as a disciple, and saw him at his door every day.

sentences.zh: 及肅卒，繁亂其配，士君子無不嘆駭，積年委棄。

translations.literal: When Liang Su died, Fan violated his mourning obligations; gentlemen were universally shocked and appalled, and for years he languished in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Su died, Li Fan violated the mourning rites owed a teacher. Gentlemen were universally shocked; for years he languished in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 後起為太常博士，太常卿權德輿奏斥之，除河南府士曹掾。

translations.literal: Later he was raised to Grand Master of Ceremonies; Grand Master of Ceremonies Quan Deyu memorialized to dismiss him, and he was appointed Registrar of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies, but Grand Master of Ceremonies Quan Deyu memorialized for his dismissal, and he was demoted to Registrar of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以其警悟異常，泌之故人為宰相，左右援拯，後得累居郡守，而力學不倦。

translations.literal: Because his intelligence was exceptionally keen, old friends of Bi who became chancellors intervened on his behalf; he later held successive prefectural posts and studied tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Because his intelligence was unusually sharp, old friends of Li Bi who had risen to the chancellorship intervened on his behalf. He eventually held successive prefectural posts and studied without cease.

sentences.zh: 罷隨州刺史，歸京師，久不承恩。

translations.literal: After leaving the Suizhou prefecture and returning to the capital, he long went without imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his post as Prefect of Suizhou and returning to the capital, he long went without imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 韋處厚入相，厚待之。

translations.literal: When Wei Chuhou entered the chancellorship, he treated Fan generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Chuhou became chancellor, he treated Li Fan with generous favor.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年六月，敬宗降誕日，御三殿，特詔兵部侍郎丁公著、太常少卿陸旦與繁等三人抗浮圖道士講論。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Baoli, on Emperor Jingzong's birthday, he held court in the Three Halls and specially ordered Vice Minister of War Ding Gongzhu, Vice Director of Ceremonies Lu Dan, and Fan, three men in all, to debate Buddhism and Daoism against monks and priests.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Baoli, on Emperor Jingzong's birthday, the emperor held court in the Three Halls and specially summoned Vice Minister of War Ding Gongzhu, Vice Director of Ceremonies Lu Dan, and Li Fan to debate Buddhist monks and Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 九月，除大理少卿，復加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Justice and additionally made Academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Justice and additionally made Academician of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 時諫官御史章疏相繼，宰臣不得已，出為亳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time memorials from remonstrance officials and censors followed in succession; the chancellors had no choice but to send him out as Prefect of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from remonstrance officials and censors poured in one after another; the chancellors had no choice but to send him out as Prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 州境嘗有群賊，剽人廬舍，劫取貨財，累政擒捕不獲。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture there had long been bandit gangs who raided dwellings and looted goods; successive administrations failed to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had long been plagued by bandits who raided homes and looted property—successive administrations had failed to capture them.

sentences.zh: 繁潛設機謀，悉知賊之巢穴，出兵盡加誅斬。

translations.literal: Fan secretly devised stratagems, learned all the bandits' hideouts, and deployed troops to execute them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan secretly devised stratagems, learned every bandit hideout, and sent troops to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 時議責繁以不先啟聞廉使，涉於擅興之罪，朝廷遣監察御史舒元輿按問。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion blamed Fan for not first notifying the surveillance commissioner, implicating him in the crime of unauthorized military action; the court dispatched Supervising Censor Shu Yuanyu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion blamed Li Fan for failing to notify the surveillance commissioner beforehand, implicating him in unauthorized military action. The court dispatched Supervising Censor Shu Yuanyu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 元輿素與繁有隙，復以初官，銳於生事，乃盡反其獄辭，以為繁濫殺無辜，狀奏，敕於京兆府賜死，時人冤之。

translations.literal: Shu Yuanyu had long held a grudge against Fan and, eager to make his mark in his first appointment, completely reversed the case testimony, claiming Fan had wantonly slaughtered the innocent; his memorial was submitted and an edict ordered execution at the Capital Prefecture—people considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanyu had long borne a grudge against Li Fan and, eager to make his mark in his first appointment, completely reversed the testimony, claiming Li Fan had wantonly slaughtered the innocent. His memorial was accepted and an edict ordered execution at the Capital Prefecture—contemporaries considered it a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 其後元輿被禍，人以為有報應焉。

translations.literal: Later Yuanyu met with disaster, and people regarded it as karmic retribution.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shu Yuanyu met with disaster himself, and people regarded it as karmic retribution.

sentences.zh: 初，泌流放江南，與柳渾、顧況為人外之交，吟詠自適。

translations.literal: Initially, when Bi was exiled to the south, he formed friendships beyond ordinary bounds with Liu Hun and Gu Kuang, composing poetry for mutual solace.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi was exiled to the south, he formed extraordinary friendships with Liu Hun and Gu Kuang, composing poetry together for mutual solace.

sentences.zh: 而渾先達，故泌復得入官於朝。

translations.literal: Liu Hun was senior, so Bi was eventually able to reenter court service.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hun was the senior of the two, and through him Li Bi was eventually able to reenter court service.

sentences.zh: 顧況者，蘇州人。

translations.literal: Gu Kuang was a native of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kuang was a native of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 能為歌詩，性詼諧，雖王公之貴與之交者，必戲侮之，然以嘲誚能文，人多狎之。

translations.literal: He could compose songs and verse; his nature was witty and humorous—even when associating with princes and nobles he would mock them, yet because his satirical wit displayed literary skill, many treated him familiarly.
translations.idiomatic: He could compose songs and verse, and his nature was witty and irreverent. Even princes and nobles who associated with him were mocked—but because his satire displayed literary brilliance, many treated him with familiar affection.

sentences.zh: 柳渾輔政，以校書郎征。

translations.literal: When Liu Hun entered government, he was summoned as Collator.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hun entered the chancellorship, Gu Kuang was summoned as Collator.

sentences.zh: 復遇李泌繼入，自謂己知秉樞要。

translations.literal: When Li Bi subsequently joined the administration, he considered himself sure to grasp the pivots of power.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi subsequently joined the administration, Gu Kuang assumed he would soon grasp the levers of power.

sentences.zh: 當得達官，久之方遷著作郎。

translations.literal: He ought to have attained high office, but only after a long wait was he promoted to Drafting Officer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He expected high office, yet only after a long wait was he promoted to Drafting Officer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 況心不樂，求歸於吳。

translations.literal: Kuang's heart was discontent; he requested return to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kuang's heart was discontent, and he petitioned to return to Wu.

sentences.zh: 而班列群官，咸有侮玩之目，皆惡嫉之。

translations.literal: Among the ranked officials in court assembly, all regarded him with contemptuous eyes and detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the ranked officials at court, all looked on him with contempt and detested him.

sentences.zh: 及泌卒，不哭，而有調笑之言，為憲司所劾，貶饒州司戶。

translations.literal: When Bi died, he did not mourn but uttered mocking words; impeached by the censorate, he was demoted to Revenue Officer of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi died, Gu Kuang did not mourn but uttered mocking words. The censorate impeached him, and he was demoted to Revenue Officer of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十捲。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings filled twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 其《贈柳宜城》辭句，率多戲劇，文體皆此類也。

translations.literal: The lines of his "Presented to Liu of Yicheng" are mostly playful in tone; his literary style was generally of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: The verses of his "Presented to Liu of Yicheng" are mostly playful in tone—his literary style was generally of this sort.

sentences.zh: 子非熊，登進士第，累佐使府，亦有詩名於時。

translations.literal: His son Feixiong passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly on mission staffs, and also had poetic renown in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feixiong passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly on mission staffs, and also won poetic renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 崔造，字玄宰，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Zao, styled Xuanzai, was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao, styled Xuanzai, was a native of Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 少涉學，永泰中，與韓會、盧東美、張正則為友，皆僑居上元，好談經濟之略，嘗以王佐自許，時人號為「四夔」。

translations.literal: In youth he studied broadly; during Yongtai, he befriended Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengzhe—all living as sojourners in Shangyuan, fond of discussing statecraft, each deeming himself fit for ministerial service; contemporaries called them the "Four Kui."
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied broadly. During the Yongtai era he befriended Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengzhe—all sojourners in Shangyuan who loved to discuss statecraft and each deemed himself fit for ministerial service. Contemporaries called them the "Four Kui."

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李棲筠引為賓僚，累至左司員外郎。

translations.literal: The Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun recruited him as staff member; he rose successively to Left Department Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun recruited him as a staff member, and he rose successively to Left Department Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 與劉晏善，及晏遭楊炎、庾准誣奏伏誅，造累貶信州長史。

translations.literal: He was close to Liu Yan; when Yan was falsely accused by Yang Yan and Yu Zhun and executed, Zao was repeatedly demoted to Long Secretary of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Liu Yan; when Yan was falsely accused by Yang Yan and Yu Zhun and executed, Cui Zao was repeatedly demoted, eventually to Long Secretary of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之逆，造為建州刺史，聞難作，馳檄鄰州，請齊舉義兵，遂調發所部，得二千人，德宗聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Zao was Prefect of Jian Prefecture; hearing of the uprising, he urgently dispatched proclamations to neighboring prefectures requesting joint raising of righteous troops, then mobilized his jurisdiction and gathered two thousand men—Dezong heard and commended this.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Cui Zao was Prefect of Jian Prefecture. Hearing of the uprising, he urgently dispatched proclamations to neighboring prefectures calling for joint righteous armies, then mobilized his jurisdiction and gathered two thousand men. Emperor Dezong heard and commended him.

sentences.zh: 及收京師，詔征造至藍田，以舅源休明逆伏誅，上疏請罪，不敢即赴闕。

translations.literal: After reclaiming the capital, an edict summoned Zao to Lantian; because his maternal uncle Yuan Xiuming had been executed for joining the rebellion, he submitted a memorial pleading guilt and dared not immediately approach court.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was reclaimed, an edict summoned Cui Zao to Lantian. Because his maternal uncle Yuan Xiuming had been executed for joining the rebellion, he submitted a memorial pleading guilt and dared not immediately approach the throne.

sentences.zh: 上以為知禮，優詔慰勉，拜吏部郎中、給事中。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this knowing propriety and issued a gracious edict of consolation and encouragement, appointing him Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Imperial Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered this an act of propriety and issued a gracious edict of consolation and encouragement, appointing him Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Imperial Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年正月，與中書舍人齊映各守本官，同平章事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan, he and Secretariat Drafter Qi Ying each retained their original posts while jointly serving as Associates of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan, he and Secretariat Drafter Qi Ying each retained their original posts while jointly serving as Associates of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時京畿兵亂之後，仍歲蝗旱，府無儲積。

translations.literal: At the time, after military turmoil in the capital region, successive years of locusts and drought left the treasury without reserves.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region, after military turmoil, had suffered successive years of locusts and drought—the treasury held no reserves.

sentences.zh: 德宗以造敢言，為能立事，故不次登用。

translations.literal: Dezong considered Zao bold in speech and capable of decisive action, hence promoted him out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong considered Cui Zao bold in speech and capable of decisive action, and promoted him out of turn.

sentences.zh: 造久從事江外，嫉錢谷諸使罔上之弊，乃奏天下兩稅錢物，委本道觀察使、本州刺史選官典部送上都；

translations.literal: Zao had long served in the Jiangnan region and resented the abuses of fiscal commissioners who deceived the throne; he memorialized that the empire's two-tax money and goods should be entrusted to each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect to select officials to escort them to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao had long served in the south and resented fiscal commissioners who deceived the throne. He memorialized that the empire's two-tax revenues should be entrusted to each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect to select officials to escort them to the capital;

sentences.zh: 諸道水陸運使及度支、巡院、江淮轉運使等並停；

translations.literal: all circuit water-and-land transport commissioners, revenues commissioners, inspection offices, and Yangzi-Huai transport commissioners were abolished;
translations.idiomatic: all circuit water-and-land transport commissioners, revenues commissioners, inspection offices, and Yangzi-Huai transport commissioners were to be abolished;

sentences.zh: 其度支、鹽鐵，委尚書省本司判；

translations.literal: revenues and salt-and-iron affairs were returned to their home ministries in the Secretariat for adjudication;
translations.idiomatic: revenues and salt-and-iron affairs were to be returned to their home ministries in the Secretariat for adjudication;

sentences.zh: 其尚書省六職，令宰臣分判。

translations.literal: the Six Ministries of the Secretariat were assigned to chancellors for divisional oversight.
translations.idiomatic: the Six Ministries of the Secretariat were to be assigned to chancellors for divisional oversight.

sentences.zh: 乃以戶部侍郎元琇判諸道鹽鐵、榷酒等事；

translations.literal: Accordingly, Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiu was assigned salt-and-iron and liquor monopoly affairs across circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiu was assigned salt-and-iron and liquor monopoly affairs across all circuits;

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎吉中孚判度支及諸道兩稅事；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Ji Zhongfu was assigned revenues and two-tax affairs across circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Ji Zhongfu was assigned revenues and two-tax affairs across all circuits;

sentences.zh: 宰臣齊映判兵部承旨及雜事；

translations.literal: Chancellor Qi Ying adjudicated the Ministry of War's Secretariat duties and miscellaneous affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Qi Ying was assigned the Ministry of War's Secretariat duties and miscellaneous affairs;

sentences.zh: 宰臣李勉判刑部；

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Mian adjudicated the Ministry of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Mian was assigned the Ministry of Justice;

sentences.zh: 宰臣劉滋判吏部、禮部；

translations.literal: Chancellor Liu Zi adjudicated the Ministries of Personnel and Rites;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Liu Zi was assigned the Ministries of Personnel and Rites;

sentences.zh: 造判戶部、工部。

translations.literal: Zao adjudicated the Ministries of Revenue and Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao was assigned the Ministries of Revenue and Works.

sentences.zh: 又以歲飢，浙江東西道入運米每年七十五萬石，今更令兩稅折納米一百萬石，委兩浙節度使韓滉運送一百萬石至東渭橋；

translations.literal: Because of famine that year, the Eastern and Western Zhejiang circuits annually contributed seven hundred fifty thousand shi of transport grain—now the two-tax was further required to deliver one million shi of rice in kind, entrusted to Zhejiang Military Commissioner Han Huang to transport one million shi to Dongwei Bridge;
translations.idiomatic: Because of famine that year, the Eastern and Western Zhejiang circuits had annually contributed seven hundred fifty thousand shi of transport grain. Now the two-tax was further required to deliver one million shi of rice in kind, entrusted to Zhejiang Military Commissioner Han Huang to transport one million shi to Dongwei Bridge;

sentences.zh: 其淮南濠壽旨米、洪潭屯米，委淮南節度使杜亞運送二十萬石至東渭橋。

translations.literal: Grain from Huainan, Hao, and Shou, and stored grain from Hong and Tan, were entrusted to Huainan Military Commissioner Du Ya to transport two hundred thousand shi to Dongwei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from Huainan, Hao, and Shou, and stored grain from Hong and Tan, were entrusted to Huainan Military Commissioner Du Ya to transport two hundred thousand shi to Dongwei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 諸道有鹽鐵處，依舊置巡院勾當；

translations.literal: In circuits with salt-and-iron operations, inspection offices were retained as before for administration;
translations.idiomatic: In circuits with salt-and-iron operations, inspection offices were to be retained as before for administration;

sentences.zh: 河陰見在米及諸道先付度支、巡院般運在路錢物，委度支依前勾當，其未離本道者，分付觀察使發遣，仍委中書門下年終類例諸道課最聞奏。

translations.literal: Rice presently at Heyin and money and goods already dispatched by revenues and inspection offices en route were entrusted to the revenues commissioner for continued administration as before; those not yet leaving their home circuits were handed to observation commissioners for dispatch—still requiring the Secretariat and Chancellery to report annual circuit performance rankings at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Rice presently stored at Heyin and money and goods already dispatched by revenues and inspection offices en route were entrusted to the revenues commissioner for continued administration as before; shipments not yet leaving their home circuits were to be handed to observation commissioners for dispatch—and the Secretariat and Chancellery were still required to report annual circuit performance rankings at year's end.

sentences.zh: 造與元琇素厚，罷使之後，以鹽鐵之任委之。

translations.literal: Zao and Yuan Xiu had long been close; after abolishing the commissioners, he entrusted salt-and-iron duties to Yuan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao and Yuan Xiu had long been close; after abolishing the commissioners, he entrusted salt-and-iron duties to Yuan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 而韓滉方司轉運，朝廷仰給其漕發。

translations.literal: But Han Huang was then managing transport—the court depended on his grain shipments.
translations.idiomatic: But Han Huang was then managing transport, and the court depended on his grain shipments.

sentences.zh: 滉以司務久行，不可遽改。

translations.literal: Huang argued that these offices had long operated and could not be abruptly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang argued that these offices had long operated and could not be abruptly changed.

sentences.zh: 德宗復以滉為江淮轉運使，余如造所條奏。

translations.literal: Dezong reappointed Huang as Yangzi-Huai Transport Commissioner; the remainder followed Zao's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong reappointed Han Huang as Yangzi-Huai Transport Commissioner; the remainder followed Cui Zao's memorial.

sentences.zh: 元琇以滉性剛難制，乃復奏江淮轉運，其江南米自江至揚子凡十八里，請滉主之；

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu considered Huang's stubborn temperament difficult to control and memorialized again on Yangzi-Huai transport: for Jiangnan grain from the river to Yangzi, eighteen li in all, he requested Huang manage it;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu considered Han Huang's stubborn temperament difficult to control and memorialized again on Yangzi-Huai transport: for Jiangnan grain from the river to Yangzi—a stretch of eighteen li—he requested that Huang manage it;

sentences.zh: 揚子已北，琇主之。

translations.literal: North of Yangzi, Xiu would manage it.
translations.idiomatic: North of Yangzi, Yuan Xiu would manage it himself.

sentences.zh: 滉聞之怒，掎摭琇鹽鐵司事論奏。

translations.literal: Huang heard this with anger and submitted impeachment memorials regarding salt-and-iron office affairs against Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang heard this with fury and submitted impeachment memorials regarding salt-and-iron office affairs against Yuan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 德宗不獲已，罷琇判使，轉尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Dezong had no choice but to remove Xiu from commissioner duties and transfer him to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had no choice but to remove Yuan Xiu from commissioner duties and transfer him to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年秋初，江淮漕米大至京師，德宗嘉其功，以滉專領度支、諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，造所條奏皆改。
