translations.literal: That autumn's beginning, transport grain from the Yangzi-Huai region arrived in great quantity at the capital; Dezong commended the achievement and put Huang solely in charge of revenues, salt-and-iron, and transport commissioners—all of Zao's memorial provisions were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, transport grain from the Yangzi-Huai region arrived in great quantity at the capital. Emperor Dezong commended the achievement and put Han Huang solely in charge of revenues, salt-and-iron, and transport commissioners—all of Cui Zao's memorial provisions were reversed.

sentences.zh: 物議亦以造所奏雖舉舊典，然凶荒之歲，難為集事，乃罷造知政事，守太子右庶子，貶琇雷州司戶。

translations.literal: Public opinion also held that although Zao's memorial revived old institutions, in years of famine and disaster it was difficult to implement; Zao was removed from governance, retained as Right Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Xiu was demoted to Revenue Officer of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that although Cui Zao's memorial revived old institutions, in years of famine and disaster it was difficult to implement. Cui Zao was removed from governance and retained as Right Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent; Yuan Xiu was demoted to Revenue Officer of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 造初奏太銳，及琇改官，憂懼成疾，數月不能視事。

translations.literal: Zao's initial memorial had been too sharp; when Xiu was transferred, anxiety and fear brought illness—for months he could not attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao's initial memorial had been too sharp; when Yuan Xiu was transferred, anxiety and fear brought illness, and for months he could not attend to his duties.

sentences.zh: 明年九月卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: The following year, in the ninth month, he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the ninth month, he died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 關播，字務元，衛州汲人也。

translations.literal: Guan Bo, courtesy name Wuyuan, was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo, courtesy name Wuyuan, was a native of Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Tianbao reign, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 鄧景山為淮南節度使，闢為從事，累授衛佐評事，遷右補闕。

translations.literal: When Deng Jingshan served as Military Commissioner of Huainan, he recruited Bo as a staff member; he was repeatedly appointed Wei Associate Reviewing Cases Officer, and was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Jingshan served as Military Commissioner of Huainan, he recruited Guan Bo onto his staff. Bo rose through successive appointments to Wei Associate Reviewing Cases Officer and then Right Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 善言物理，尤精釋氏之學。

translations.literal: He was skilled at discussing the principles of things and was especially accomplished in Buddhist learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at discourse on natural principle and was especially accomplished in Buddhist learning.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，神策軍使王駕鶴妻關氏以播與同宗，深遇之。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, the wife of Shence Army Commissioner Wang Jihe, the Lady Guan, because Bo shared her clan surname, treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign, Lady Guan, wife of Shence Army Commissioner Wang Jihe, treated Guan Bo with exceptional favor on account of their shared clan affiliation.

sentences.zh: 元載惡其交往，出為河南府兵曹，攝職數縣，皆有政能。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai resented his association with them and sent him out as Military Staff Officer of Henan Prefecture; acting in the duties of several counties, in all cases he showed administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai resented these connections and had him posted as Military Staff Officer of Henan Prefecture. Serving in acting capacity over several counties, he displayed genuine administrative talent in each.

sentences.zh: 陳少游領浙東、淮南，又闢為判官，歷檢校金部員外，攝滁州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou controlled Zhedong and Huainan and again recruited him as adjutant; he successively served as Acting Secretary of the Ministry of Revenue and Acting Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shaoyou held authority over Zhedong and Huainan, he recruited Guan Bo again as adjutant. Bo served successively as Acting Secretary of the Ministry of Revenue and Acting Prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜阻兵，跋扈於梁汴。

translations.literal: Li Lingyao obstructed with arms and was overbearing in Liang and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao raised arms in defiance and behaved with arrogance throughout the Liang and Bian region.

sentences.zh: 少游自總兵鎮淮上，所在盜賊峰起。

translations.literal: Shaoyou personally commanded troops garrisoning the Huai region; wherever he was, bandits rose like peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou personally held overall military command on the Huai front, and banditry erupted wherever his forces were stationed.

sentences.zh: 播調閱州兵，令其守備。

translations.literal: Bo inspected and reviewed the prefectural troops and ordered them to guard and prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo inspected the prefectural troops and organized them for defense.

sentences.zh: 又為政清淨簡惠，既無盜賊，人甚安之。

translations.literal: Moreover his governance was pure, quiet, simple, and benevolent; once bandits were gone, the people were greatly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was clean, restrained, and mild. With banditry suppressed, the people enjoyed genuine peace.

sentences.zh: 楊綰、常袞知政事，薦播為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Yang Wan and Chang Gun directed state affairs and recommended Bo as Secretary of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wan and Chang Gun directed state affairs, they recommended Guan Bo for appointment as Secretary of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 德宗登極，湖南山洞中有王國良者，聚眾為盜，令播往宣撫之。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, in the mountain caves of Hunan there was one Wang Guoliang who gathered a crowd and became a bandit; he ordered Bo to go and proclaim soothing policies to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, a man named Wang Guoliang had gathered followers in the mountain caves of Hunan and turned to banditry. The emperor dispatched Guan Bo to proclaim imperial goodwill and attempt pacification.

sentences.zh: 臨行，召對於別殿，上問政理之要，播奏云：「為政之本，需求有道賢人，乃可得理。

translations.literal: Before departure, he was summoned for audience in a separate hall; the emperor asked the essentials of governance, and Bo memorialized saying: "The root of governing lies in seeking men of the Way who are virtuous—only then can order be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure, he was summoned to audience in a side hall. When the emperor asked what lay at the heart of good governance, Guan Bo replied, "The foundation of government is to seek out virtuous men who truly understand the Way. Only then can the realm be well governed.

sentences.zh: 」上謂播云：「朕下詔求賢良，當躬新閱試，亦遣使臣黜陟，廣加搜訪聞薦，擢其能者用之，冀以傅理。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Bo: "I have issued edicts seeking the worthy and good; I myself shall personally conduct fresh examinations, and also dispatch commissioners for promotion and demotion, broadly searching, inquiring, and recommending, promoting the capable to use them, hoping thereby to assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Guan Bo, "I have already issued edicts seeking worthy men. I intend to examine candidates personally, dispatch commissioners to conduct promotions and demotions, and launch a broad search through recommendations—raising the capable to office in the hope of putting the realm in order.

sentences.zh: 」播奏曰：「下詔求賢黜陟舉薦，唯得求名詞之士，安有有道賢人肯隨牒舉選乎？

translations.literal: Bo memorialized: "Issuing edicts to seek the worthy, with promotion and demotion through recommendation—one can only obtain men who seek reputation and elegant phrasing; how could there be virtuous men of the Way willing to follow documents and enter examinations?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo replied, "Edicts for seeking talent, promotions and demotions, and recommendations will yield only men who chase reputation and fine phrases. What man of genuine virtue and understanding would stoop to enter the examination lists?"

sentences.zh: 」上悅其言，謂播曰：「卿且使去，回日當與卿論政事。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with his words and said to Bo: "You go on your mission for now; when you return we shall discuss state affairs together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and told Guan Bo, "Go now on your mission. When you return, we shall discuss affairs of state together."

sentences.zh: 」播又奏曰：「臣今奏詔招撫，國良不受命，臣請便宣恩命，語鄰境速出兵翦除。

translations.literal: Bo further memorialized: "Your subject now goes by edict to win over and soothe; if Guoliang does not accept the command, your subject requests to proclaim the gracious decree forthwith and tell neighboring circuits to speedily dispatch troops to cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo added, "If Wang Guoliang refuses the imperial command when I arrive to pacify him, I ask permission to proclaim your grace on the spot and notify neighboring circuits to send troops at once to destroy him."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言深合朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words deeply accord with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words accord deeply with my intent."

sentences.zh: 」使回，改兵部員外，遷河中少尹。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was changed to Secretary of the Ministry of War and promoted to Vice Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission, he was appointed Secretary of the Ministry of War and promoted to Vice Governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 建中初，張鎰為河中少尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Zhang Yi was Vice Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong reign, Zhang Yi served as Vice Governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 鎰尋入相，二年七月，遷播給事中。

translations.literal: Yi soon entered the chancellorship; in the seventh month of the second year, Bo was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi soon entered the chancellorship. In the seventh month of Jianzhong 2, Guan Bo was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 舊例，諸司甲庫，皆是胥吏掌知，為弊頗久，播始建議並以士人知之，至今稱當。

translations.literal: By old precedent, the archives of the various offices were all managed by clerks and runners—a abuse long standing; Bo first proposed that gentlemen-scholars manage them jointly, and to this day it is called appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding custom, the personnel archives of the various ministries had been managed by low-level clerks—a source of chronic abuse. Guan Bo was the first to propose placing educated officials in charge of them, a reform still praised as apt.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎、奉迎皇太后副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Commissioner for Welcoming the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Commissioner for Welcoming the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 盧杞以播柔緩，冀其易制，驟稱薦之。

translations.literal: Lu Qi, because Bo was gentle and mild, hoped he would be easy to control and abruptly praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, judging Guan Bo gentle and pliable, hoped to control him easily and suddenly began praising and recommending him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部侍郎，轉刑部尚書、知刪定。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Justice and placed in charge of statutory revision.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Justice with charge over statutory revision.

sentences.zh: 奏上元中，詔擇古今名將十人於武成王廟配享，如文宣王廟之儀。

translations.literal: He memorialized that in the Shangyuan era an edict had chosen ten famous generals from ancient and modern times for companion worship at the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, following the ritual of the Temple of the Literary Sage King.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that during the Shangyuan reign an edict had selected ten famous generals from history for companion worship in the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, patterned after the rites of Confucius's temple.

sentences.zh: 播以「太公古稱大賢，今其下稱亞聖，於義不安。

translations.literal: Bo argued: "The Grand Duke was anciently called a great sage; now beneath him they are called sub-sages—in propriety this is unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo argued, "The Grand Duke was called a great sage in antiquity; to designate those beneath him as 'lesser sages' is improper in principle.

sentences.zh: 又孔子十哲，皆是當時弟子，今所擇名將，年代不同，於義既乖，於事又失。

translations.literal: Moreover Confucius's Ten Worthies were all disciples of his own time; the famous generals now chosen belong to different ages—in principle this already conflicts, and in practice it is also wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Confucius's Ten Worthies were all disciples of his own day. The generals now chosen belong to different ages. This violates principle and misses the point in practice as well.

sentences.zh: 臣請刪去名將配享之儀及十哲之稱。

translations.literal: Your subject requests deletion of the rite of companion worship for famous generals and the title of Ten Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore request that the rite of companion worship for famous generals and the designation 'Ten Worthies' be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 建中三年十月，拜銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事、集賢殿崇文館大學士、修國史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Jianzhong, he was appointed Silver-and-Purple Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall and Chongwen Pavilion, and Compiler of National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianzhong 3, he was appointed Silver-and-Purple Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall and Chongwen Pavilion, and Compiler of National History.

sentences.zh: 時政事決在盧杞，播但斂衽取容而已。

translations.literal: At the time state affairs were decided by Lu Qi; Bo only drew in his robes and sought to please, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lu Qi held decisive power over state affairs. Guan Bo did nothing but compose himself and curry favor.

sentences.zh: 乏於知人之鑑，好大言虛誕者，播必悅而親信之。

translations.literal: Lacking the mirror of discerning men, those who loved grand talk and empty extravagance—Bo was sure to be pleased and personally trust them.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked the discernment to judge men. Those who loved grandiose and fantastic talk always won his pleasure and personal trust.

sentences.zh: 有李元平、陶公達、張愻、劉承誡，皆言談詭妄，讠誇大可立功名，亦有微材薄藝。

translations.literal: There were Li Yuanping, Tao Gongda, Zhang Sun, and Liu Chengjie—all spoke in strange and absurd ways, boasting that great merit and fame could quickly be established, though they did possess slight talent and meager skills.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were Li Yuanping, Tao Gongda, Zhang Sun, and Liu Chengjie—all given to strange and extravagant talk, boasting that great feats and lasting fame could be won at a stroke, though each possessed at best modest talent and slender skill.

sentences.zh: 播累奏雲元平等皆可將相也，請閱試用之，上以為然，以元平為補闕。

translations.literal: Bo repeatedly memorialized saying Yuanping and the others could all serve as generals and chancellors, requesting examination and trial use; the emperor approved, and Yuanping was made Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo repeatedly memorialized that Yuanping and the others were fit for generalship and the chancellorship, and asked that they be examined and put to use. The emperor agreed, and Li Yuanping was appointed Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 會淮西節度李希烈叛亂，上以汝州要鎮，令選擇刺史。

translations.literal: When Huai West Military Commissioner Li Xilie rebelled, the emperor, because Ruzhou was a strategic fortress, ordered selection of a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie, Military Commissioner of Huai West, rose in rebellion, the emperor ordered that a prefect be chosen for Ruzhou, a city of critical strategic importance.

sentences.zh: 播薦元平為汝州刺史，尋加檢校吏部郎中、汝州別駕，知州事。

translations.literal: Bo recommended Yuanping as Prefect of Ruzhou; soon he was additionally made Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, and entrusted with prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo recommended Li Yuanping as Prefect of Ruzhou. He was soon given additional titles as Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, with charge over the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元平至州旬日，為希烈所擒，汝州陷賊，中外哂之。

translations.literal: Yuanping reached the prefecture for ten days and was captured by Xilie; Ruzhou fell to the rebels, and court and countryside mocked them.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days of Li Yuanping's arrival, Li Xilie captured him and Ruzhou fell to the rebels. Court and country alike laughed at the debacle.

sentences.zh: 由是公達等未克任用。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gongda and the others were unable to be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, Tao Gongda and the others never received appointment.

sentences.zh: 播與盧杞等從駕幸奉天，既而杞、白志貞等並貶黜，播尚知政事，中外囂然，以為不可，遂罷相，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Bo followed the imperial carriage with Lu Qi and others in fleeing to Fengtian; afterward Qi, Bai Zhizhen, and others were all demoted and dismissed, yet Bo still directed state affairs—court and countryside were in uproar, holding this unacceptable; he was then removed as chancellor and changed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo accompanied the emperor's flight to Fengtian along with Lu Qi and others. After Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, and the rest were demoted and dismissed, Guan Bo nevertheless remained in charge of state affairs. Uproar spread through court and country at the seeming injustice, and he was removed from the chancellorship and made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 大臣韋倫等泣於朝曰：「宰相不能謀猷翊贊，以至今日，而尚為尚書，可痛心也！」

translations.literal: Great minister Wei Lun and others wept at court saying: "The chancellor could not plan strategy and assist in support, reaching even to this day, yet still holds the post of minister—this is heartbreaking!"
translations.idiomatic: Senior minister Wei Lun and others wept openly at court, saying, "The chancellor could neither counsel wisely nor lend proper support, and brought us to this pass—yet he still holds a ministerial post. The pain of it is unbearable!"

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，回紇請和親，以咸安公主出降可汗，令播以本官加檢校右僕射、兼御史大夫，持節充送咸安公主及冊可汗使，奉使往來，皆清儉謹慎，蕃人悅之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, the Uyghurs requested a marriage alliance; Princess Xian'an was sent down to marry the khan; Bo was ordered, with his existing office, additionally Acting Right Vice Director and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, bearing the staff as Commissioner for Escorting Princess Xian'an and Enfeoffing the Khan; on mission going and returning, in all cases he was pure, frugal, careful, and cautious—the frontier peoples were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4, the Uyghurs sought a marriage alliance, and Princess Xian'an was sent to wed the khan. Guan Bo was ordered to retain his existing rank while additionally serving as Acting Right Vice Director and Censor-in-Chief, and was dispatched with imperial credentials as Commissioner for Escorting Princess Xian'an and Enfeoffing the Khan. Throughout his mission he conducted himself with frugal integrity and careful restraint, winning the goodwill of the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 使回，遷兵部尚書，固辭疾，請罷官，改太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was promoted to Minister of War; he firmly declined citing illness and requested dismissal from office; he was changed to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Minister of War, but he firmly pleaded illness and asked to leave office. He was then made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 播致仕之後，減去僮僕車騎，閉關守靜，不縈外事，士君子重之。

translations.literal: After Bo's retirement, he reduced servants, carriages, and escorts, withdrew behind closed doors to keep quiet, and did not entangle himself in outside affairs—gentlemen esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: After his retirement, Guan Bo reduced his household staff, carriages, and escorts, withdrew into seclusion, and shunned outside affairs. Men of honor held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 貞元十三年正月卒，時年七十九，廢朝一日，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-nine at the time; court mourning was suspended for one day; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of Zhenyuan 13, at the age of seventy-nine. Court business was suspended for one day of mourning, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 李元平者，宗室子。

translations.literal: Li Yuanping was a member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanping was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 始為湖南觀察使蕭復判官，試大理評事。

translations.literal: At first he served as adjutant to Hunan Observation Commissioner Xiao Fu, probationary as Grand Court Reviewing Cases Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He began as adjutant to Hunan Observation Commissioner Xiao Fu, serving provisionally as Grand Court Reviewing Cases Officer.

sentences.zh: 性疏傲，敢大言，好論兵，天下賢士大夫無可其意者，以是人多銜怒。

translations.literal: By nature he was careless and arrogant, dared grand talk, loved discussing military affairs; worthy gentlemen and grand masters throughout the realm could satisfy none of his opinions—thus many bore resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was casual and arrogant, bold in extravagant speech, and fond of holding forth on military matters. No worthy scholar or official in the realm could satisfy him, and many nursed resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 關播奇重之，許以將帥。

translations.literal: Guan Bo found him extraordinary and treated him with great regard, promising him the rank of general or marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo regarded him as a marvel and treated him with exceptional favor, promising him a commander's post.

sentences.zh: 時希烈反叛，朝廷以汝州與賊接壤，刺史韋光裔懦弱不任職，播乃盛稱元平，特召見，超左補闕，不數日，擢為檢校吏部郎中，兼汝州別駕，知州事。

translations.literal: At the time Xilie rebelled; the court because Ruzhou bordered the rebels, and Prefect Wei Guangyi was weak and incompetent in office, Bo then lavishly praised Yuanping, had him specially summoned for audience, promoted him over the Left Remonstrance Official, within not many days raised him to Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, knowing prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, the court judged Ruzhou critical because it bordered rebel territory, while Prefect Wei Guangyi was too weak for the post. Guan Bo lavishly praised Li Yuanping, had him specially summoned to audience, leapfrogged him to Left Remonstrance Official, and within days elevated him to Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, with charge over the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既至部，募工徒繕理郛郭，希烈乃使勇士應募，執役板築，凡入數百人，元平不之覺。

translations.literal: Once he reached his jurisdiction, he recruited laborers to repair the outer walls; Xilie then sent brave warriors to answer the recruitment, performing corvée labor in earth and board construction—in all several hundred entered, and Yuanping did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, he recruited laborers to repair the city walls. Li Xilie sent bold warriors to enlist as laborers for earthwork and construction. Several hundred entered the city in this way, and Li Yuanping noticed nothing amiss.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣偽將李克誠以數百騎突至其城，先應募執役者應於內，縛元平馳去。

translations.literal: Xilie dispatched the fake general Li Kecheng with several hundred horsemen to burst suddenly upon the city; those who had earlier answered recruitment for corvée responded from within, bound Yuanping and rode off with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie sent the rebel general Li Kecheng with several hundred horsemen in a sudden assault on the city. The men who had enlisted earlier as laborers responded from within, seized Li Yuanping, and galloped away with him.

sentences.zh: 既見希烈，遺下污地。

translations.literal: Once he saw Xilie, he left filth on the ground below.
translations.idiomatic: When brought before Li Xilie, he lost control of his bowels on the spot.

sentences.zh: 希烈見其無須眇小，戲謂克誠曰：「使汝取李元平，何得將元平兒來？

translations.literal: Xilie, seeing him beardless and slight and small, jestingly said to Kecheng: "I sent you to take Li Yuanping—how did you end up bringing Li Yuanping's boy?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie, seeing that he was beardless and slight of build, jokingly said to Li Kecheng, "I sent you to capture Li Yuanping—why have you brought me Li Yuanping's boy instead?"

sentences.zh: 」因嫚罵曰：「盲宰相使汝當我，何待我淺耶！

translations.literal: He then reviled him with contempt saying: "A blind chancellor sent you to face me—why treat me so shallowly!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he cursed in contempt, "Your blind chancellor sent you to oppose me—is that not treating me far too lightly!"

sentences.zh: 」偽署為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was falsely appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie falsely appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 播聞元平得用，仍欺於人曰：「李生功業濟矣。

translations.literal: Bo heard Yuanping had been put to use and still deceived people saying: "Master Li's achievements are about to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Bo heard that Li Yuanping had been given office, he still deceived others, saying, "Young Li's great work is nearly accomplished."

sentences.zh: 」言必能覆希烈而建功也。

translations.literal: His words meant that he would surely be able to overthrow Xilie and establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that Li Yuanping would surely overthrow Li Xilie and win lasting glory.

sentences.zh: 居無何，希烈用為宰相，或告其有二者，乃斷一指以自誓。

translations.literal: Before long, Xilie used him as chancellor; someone reported that he had dual loyalty, whereupon he cut off a finger to swear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Xilie appointed him chancellor. When someone accused him of divided loyalty, he severed a finger to swear his fidelity.

sentences.zh: 希烈既死，或有人言在賊中微有謀慮，貸死流於珍州。

translations.literal: Once Xilie died, someone said that while among the rebels he had slight planning and consideration; his death sentence was commuted and he was exiled to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xilie died, someone reported that he had shown some measure of strategic judgment while serving the rebels. His death sentence was commuted and he was exiled to Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會赦得歸剡中，浙東觀察使皇甫政表聞其到，以發上怒，復流賀州而死。

translations.literal: When an amnesty permitted return to Shanzhong, Zhedong Observation Commissioner Huangfu Zheng memorialized reporting his arrival, arousing the emperor's anger; he was again exiled to He Prefecture and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty allowed him to return to Shan, Zhedong Observation Commissioner Huangfu Zheng memorialized reporting his arrival, which provoked the emperor's wrath. He was exiled again to He Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：蒸嘗礿祀，前王制以奉先；

translations.literal: The historian comments: Steam offerings, sacrificial feasts, and autumn offerings—the institutions of former kings for serving the ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Steam offerings, sacrificial feasts, and autumn rites—these were the institutions of the ancient kings for honoring the ancestors;

sentences.zh: 怪力亂神，宣聖鄙而不語。

translations.literal: Strange power, disorder, and spirits—the Propagating Sage despised these and did not speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: Tales of marvels, violence, spirits, and chaos—the Sage himself held them in contempt and would not discuss them.

sentences.zh: 凡雲左道，固有舊章。

translations.literal: Generally speaking of heterodox ways, there have always been old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Heterodox practices have always been regulated by ancient law.

sentences.zh: 玙假於鬼神，乃至將相，既處代天之位，爰滋亂政之源。

translations.literal: Yu relied on ghosts and spirits, even reaching the rank of general and chancellor; having already occupied the position of acting for Heaven, he thereby nourished the source of disorder in government.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu relied on ghosts and spirits to rise even to generalship and the chancellorship. Having taken a position that stood in for Heaven itself, he became a wellspring of disorder in government.

sentences.zh: 國禎妖人疑眾，妄恢其祀典；

translations.literal: Guozhen the sorcerer deceived the multitude and recklessly expanded the sacrificial canon;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen, a sorcerer who deluded the people, presumptuously expanded the state cult;

sentences.zh: 梁鎮正士抗疏，方悟其上心。

translations.literal: Liang Zhen the upright man submitted a forthright memorial, and only then was the sovereign's true intent understood.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the upright Liang Zhen submitted a bold remonstrance did the throne grasp what the emperor truly intended.

sentences.zh: 泌見可進而知難退，足為高率智辯之士；

translations.literal: Bi saw what could be advanced and knew the difficulty of withdrawal—sufficient to be called a lofty, frank, wise, and eloquent man;
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi knew when to advance and when to withdraw—a man lofty in bearing, direct in manner, and sharp in mind;

sentences.zh: 居相位而談鬼神，乃見狂妄浮薄之蹤。

translations.literal: Occupying the chancellorship yet talking of ghosts and spirits—thus were revealed the traces of wild arrogance and frivolous shallowness.
translations.idiomatic: yet he spoke of ghosts and spirits while holding the chancellorship, revealing the mark of rash and shallow conceit.

sentences.zh: 《王制》云：「執左道以亂政，殺。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: "Those who adhere to heterodox ways to disorder government—kill them."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites states, "Whoever persists in heterodox practices to subvert government shall be put to death."

sentences.zh: 」寧無畏乎！

translations.literal: Can one not fear this!
translations.idiomatic: Should they not have trembled before such a law?

sentences.zh: 繁之醜行，棄於當時，竟陷非辜，諒由素履。

translations.literal: Fan's ugly conduct was cast off in his own time; he ultimately fell into unjust guilt—no doubt because of his lifelong conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan's disgraceful conduct was condemned in his own day; that he ultimately suffered unjust punishment reflects, no doubt, the life he had lived.

sentences.zh: 造為臣得禮，蒞事非能；

translations.literal: Zao as minister attained ritual propriety, yet was not capable in presiding over affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao understood ritual propriety as a minister, yet lacked capacity to manage affairs;

sentences.zh: 播居位取容，舉人敗事。

translations.literal: Bo held office seeking to please; in recommending men he ruined affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo held office only to curry favor, and the men he recommended brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 皆非國器，咸歷台司，失人者亡，國其危矣。

translations.literal: None were vessels of state, yet all passed through high offices; he who loses men perishes—the state was indeed in peril.
translations.idiomatic: None was fit to bear the weight of empire, yet all rose to the highest offices. When a ruler loses the right men, ruin follows—and the state stood in peril.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：玙、泌、造、播，俱非相材。

translations.literal: In praise: Yu, Bi, Zao, and Bo—none possessed the timber of chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Wang Yu, Li Bi, Cui Zao, and Guan Bo—none possessed the makings of a true chancellor.

sentences.zh: 國禎左道，梁生直哉！

translations.literal: Guozhen's heterodox way; Scholar Liang was upright indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen walked the path of heterodoxy; Scholar Liang was upright indeed!
